privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: How SquareCampus gathers, safeguards, and shares personal data for schools and colleges.

sections.title: 1. Company & Data Fiduciary
sections.html:
Effective 21 November 2026 · Revision 2026-11-21.1

SquareCampus™ is a trademark (registration pending) of Fairhelm Systems (OPC) Private Limited. All services are provided by Fairhelm Systems (OPC) Private Limited, unless otherwise stated in a written agreement or order form.

References to "SquareCampus" in this Policy mean Fairhelm Systems (OPC) Private Limited.

FAIRHELM SYSTEMS (OPC) PRIVATE LIMITEDRegistered office: No. 33, 4th Floor, 1st Main, Road 3, Ganganagar, R T Nagar, Bangalore North, Bangalore – 560032, Karnataka, IndiaCIN: U62099KA2026OPC225579 · Incorporated in India on 5 August 2026 under the Companies Act, 2013 · One Person CompanyGSTIN: 29AAHCF1819L1ZA · Registered under the Goods and Services Tax, KarnatakaEmail: contact@squarecampus.com

Fairhelm decides how to handle website enquiries, business contacts, billing and its own legal obligations. For those purposes it is the Data Fiduciary. When a school or college determines how to use its students’, guardians’ or staff records, the Institution is the Data Fiduciary and Fairhelm processes those records on its documented instructions. The Institution’s notice explains its choices. Our Data Processing Addendum sets the limits on ours.

The service is offered on an India-only basis for institutional customer data. Before activation we and the Institution must document the providers, processing locations, backups and support access needed to meet that restriction. A workflow that cannot meet it must remain disabled. Website enquiries and business correspondence follow the arrangements described below.

sections.title: 2. Information We Collect
sections.html:
2.1 Institution Information

We may collect or receive details about the Institution, including:

  • Institution name, type, and registered address;
  • Administrative contacts, emails, and phone numbers;
  • Billing preferences and subscription configurations;
  • Modules, features, and integrations selected by the Institution.

2.2 User Information

We receive, process, or store data about individual users, such as:

  • Names, contact details, roles (student, parent, educator, staff);
  • Authentication records and hashed login credentials;
  • Academic data, attendance, assignments, assessments, and grades;
  • Messages, notifications, and collaboration history generated inside the Service.

2.3 Technical and Usage Data

Automatic information we collect includes:

  • IP address, device, and browser metadata;
  • Pages, modules, and features accessed with timestamps;
  • Diagnostic logs, error events, and performance telemetry;
  • Cookies or tokens used for authentication and session management.

2.4 Sensitive Data and Minors

SquareCampus may process information about minors (students) and data that may be considered sensitive (photographs, health records, disciplinary notes) strictly under the Institution's instructions.

Institutions are responsible for obtaining any necessary parental or guardian permissions before submitting such data through the Service.

For an enquiry or pilot request we may receive your organisation, contact details, message and communication choices. Where we use AI to help answer an enquiry, its purpose is to draft or send a routine reply. You can request a human reply by email. The intake uses IP and browser details to protect the form and may use challenge answers, input method, timing and pointer movement for abuse prevention. The enquiry may reach our customer-relationship system and team email. Where the form opens an email draft, you decide whether to send it using your mail provider. Please keep student records and other sensitive information out of an enquiry.

sections.title: 3. How We Use the Information
sections.html:
We use enquiry details to reply and assess the requested engagement. Where we offer optional marketing, that choice is separate. You may withdraw it using the contact below. Technical signals protect delivery and help detect abuse. Billing records support invoicing, accounting and legal obligations.

Within the product, account identifiers enable access, academic records support the workflows selected by the Institution, guardian details enable authorised communications, and access logs support security and accountability. We may use aggregate statistics for product planning only when individuals cannot reasonably be identified. We do not sell personal data.

sections.title: 4. Legal Basis for Processing
sections.html:
For our own processing we identify the purpose and applicable legal authority. As the relevant provisions of India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) take effect, we rely on consent or a specific use permitted under section 7 where its conditions apply. For example, we may use information voluntarily supplied to reply to the enquiry for which you provided it. An unrelated purpose requiring consent needs a separate affirmative choice.

An institutional contract defines our instructions. The Institution is responsible for the authority to collect and use each category of personal data. Where consent is required it must give the applicable notice and obtain and record that consent.

Where Fairhelm seeks consent, we will give the applicable notice at the point of collection and offer the language choices required by law as those provisions commence. For an accessible notice, a language request or help withdrawing consent, email privacy@squarecampus.com.

sections.title: 5. Data Sharing and Transfers
sections.html:
Authorised personnel and contracted providers receive the information necessary for their functions. These may include hosting, backup, messaging, customer support, enquiry management and email. Professional advisers may receive information under confidentiality obligations. We may disclose information where required by law. The signed processing schedule identifies providers and locations for institutional data. Ask privacy@squarecampus.com for the applicable list.

Institutional instructions and the Data Processing Addendum govern any provider processing student or staff data. An institution-directed disclosure and a vendor acting on our behalf can have different purposes and responsibilities.

sections.title: 6. Data Security
sections.html:
For institutional processing the agreed safeguards include access controls, encryption in transit and at rest, monitoring and backup procedures. Report a suspected incident to security@squarecampus.com. Please identify the service and time and omit credentials and unnecessary personal records.

When we process for a school, we alert its incident contact without undue delay, provide the facts available and send updates. Each party remains responsible for any report it must make directly, including a reportable incident under the CERT-In Directions. When Fairhelm itself determines the purpose, it takes responsibility for applicable notifications. Once Rule 7 of the DPDP Rules, 2025 applies, this includes notifying affected people and initially informing the Board without delay, with details to the Board within 72 hours of awareness unless it allows more time.

sections.title: 7. Data Retention
sections.html:
For institutional records, the order form and processing schedule specify return, deletion, backup expiry and applicable legal holds. An authorised school contact can request preservation or export at support@squarecampus.com. Our Data Retention page describes the available process and its limits.

For website enquiries, copies may exist in the enquiry system, team email and security logs. We have yet to adopt a fixed enquiry retention period. On a request we assess whether the enquiry or a legal obligation still requires each copy and handle erasure requests at privacy@squarecampus.com. Security records subject to a mandatory preservation period are restricted to their continuing purpose.

sections.title: 8. Your Rights as a Data Principal
sections.html:
Write to privacy@squarecampus.com to ask what personal data we use for our own purposes, request correction or erasure, withdraw consent, nominate a representative for death or incapacity, or raise a grievance. Identify the request and the account or enquiry concerned without including passwords or entire student records. We may ask for proportionate evidence of identity or authority. We explain the outcome and any lawful reason to retain information.

When the relevant DPDP provisions commence, statutory rights include access to a summary of processing and recipients subject to statutory exceptions, correction, completion, updating, erasure, grievance redressal and nomination, on the conditions in sections 11–14. Withdrawal does not affect lawful prior processing. If other law requires us to retain a record, we explain the restriction.

For school-held records, contact the school first. If you write to us, we will route the request to the appropriate institutional contact and assist on instructions. A guardian may act for a child subject to verification of authority.

If you are acting as a lawful guardian for a person with a disability, we will verify the appointment and its scope where required. We will not assume that disability alone gives another person authority to act.
sections.navigationLabel: Your Rights as a Data Principal

sections.title: 9. Cookies and Similar Technologies
sections.html: Cookies and similar identifiers support authentication, session persistence, and preference storage. We do not use third-party advertising cookies in the core academic and administrative areas.

sections.title: 10. Children’s and Student Data
sections.html:
A child is a person under eighteen for the DPDP Act. The school decides which student workflows to enable and must give families the applicable notice. Where required, it must verify and record consent from a parent or lawful guardian before processing, and communicate changes or withdrawal to us. A child’s login cannot authorise the school’s contract or substitute for required parental consent.

Section 9 and Rules 10–12 take effect in the later commencement phase. The Fourth Schedule contains a limited exception for an educational institution undertaking specified educational or enrolled-child safety activities, subject to its conditions. The Institution must document any applicable exception for the particular activity. Fairhelm cannot rely on school status for independent commercial purposes.

We run no advertising technology in the product. We do not target children with advertising, use their identifiable behaviour for commercial profiling, or train AI models on student or child data. School-directed attendance, academic and safety records are used for the authorised institutional purpose. A general AI authorisation cannot override these limits. We will decline instructions likely to harm a child’s well-being.

sections.title: 11. Grievance Redressal
sections.html:
The founder currently handles grievances for Fairhelm. Write to the Grievance Officer at privacy@squarecampus.com or to the registered office in section 1. We acknowledge receipt and address grievances expeditiously and within one month of receipt, or sooner where law requires. This is also our service commitment while DPDP provisions take effect.

Where the DPDP complaint provisions apply, you may approach the Data Protection Board of India after exhausting the applicable grievance process. For school-controlled records start with the Institution. You can also use any remedy already available to you under applicable law.

sections.title: 12. Changes to This Policy
sections.html:
We will identify the revision and give a clear notice of material changes before applying them to a new purpose. Where that purpose needs consent, we will ask for it. Withdrawal is available through the same consent channel where offered or by writing to privacy@squarecampus.com.

The Government notified phased commencement of the DPDP Act and Rules in November 2025. As of this revision, the main notice, children’s data, breach and individual-rights provisions are scheduled for May 2027. We distinguish the practices we offer today from statutory rights as they take effect.

sections.html:
Effective 21 November 2026 · Revision 2026-11-21.1

SquareCampus™ is a trademark (registration pending) of Fairhelm Systems (OPC) Private Limited. All services are provided by Fairhelm Systems (OPC) Private Limited, unless otherwise stated in a written agreement or order form.

The contracting parties are Fairhelm and the Institution identified in a pilot or subscription order signed by an authorised adult representative. The order incorporates the identified revision of these Terms and the Data Processing Addendum for institutional personal data. The DPA governs processing. Expressly negotiated terms govern their stated subject, subject to the DPA’s priority clause and mandatory law. The Privacy Policy describes our data practices.

Staff, students and guardians are authorised users subject to the access and conduct rules. A student’s or guardian’s use alone creates no institutional payment, indemnity or signing obligation. The Institution gives users age-appropriate instructions and manages access.

sections.title: 2. Description of the Service
sections.html:
SquareCampus is a SaaS platform for schools, colleges, and other educational institutions to manage admissions, attendance, grades, examinations, fees, communication, and related academic workflows.

The signed order identifies the modules available to the Institution. We may maintain and improve them. Removing a material contracted capability requires an agreed alternative or the termination and refund remedies in these Terms.

sections.title: 3. Account Registration and Security
sections.html:
Give each authorised user their own credentials and only the access appropriate to their role. The Institution manages enrolment, guardian authority, access reviews and prompt revocation. Users must protect their credentials. Shared institutional logins, disclosure to competitors and unauthorised third-party access are prohibited.

Notify security@squarecampus.com promptly on suspected compromise. Each party is responsible to the extent its conduct caused the loss, subject to section 14. On reasonable notice the Institution will provide relevant access records for an investigation, with unrelated information protected. Immediate restrictions must be proportionate to the threat.

sections.title: 4. License and Permitted Use
sections.html:
Subject to these Terms and any applicable order form, SquareCampus grants Institutions a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, and non-sublicensable license to use the Service for internal educational and administrative purposes during the agreed term, subject to the suspension and termination provisions.

Unless expressly permitted, you must not:

  • Copy, modify, or derive works from the Service;
  • Reverse engineer or attempt to extract the platform source code;
  • Resell or re-distribute the Service outside your Institution;
  • Use the Service to build a competing product;
  • Circumvent usage limits, quotas, or licensing restrictions; or
  • Use the Service in violation of applicable laws or regulations.

sections.title: 5. Subscription, Fees, and Billing
sections.html:
The signed order specifies the term, activation, fees, GST, payment dates, enrolment measure, approved usage charges, and any true-up. The SquareCampus Founding Institutional Pilot for 2026–27 has a one-time fee of ₹50,000 plus applicable GST, payable upfront against invoice. Access begins on the agreed date after signature and confirmed payment, and ends on 31 March 2027 at 23:59 IST. The pilot does not renew automatically. A subsequent subscription requires a new written order. The separate Selected Institutional Launch Pilot carries no platform subscription charge where the Institution is expressly approved for that programme. Subscription renewals follow the signed subscription order.

Advance fees are payable as agreed. On cancellation for convenience, fees for the current committed term remain payable. The Cancellation and Refund Policy governs eligible refunds, including the unserved portion after an uncured material failure by SquareCampus. A disputed invoice must identify the disputed amount and reason. The Institution pays the undisputed balance while the parties review the difference.

sections.title: 6. Data Ownership and Rights
sections.html:
The Institution retains its rights in the records it supplies and the institutional records generated for it. Individuals retain their legal rights in their personal data. The Institution grants Fairhelm the permission needed to provide, secure and support the ordered service under the DPA.

Fairhelm owns the platform and may use aggregate statistics that do not reasonably identify an individual or disclose the Institution’s confidential information. Account-linked telemetry remains subject to the DPA when processed on institutional instructions. Neither party may re-identify anonymised statistics.

The Institution may request its records during the term and through the exit process in the Data Processing Addendum. The order specifies formats, timing, handover and any agreed charges before processing begins.

sections.title: 7. Privacy and Data Protection
sections.html:
The Privacy Policy describes Fairhelm’s own processing and its institutional role. The Data Processing Addendum applies to personal data handled for the Institution, including during a pilot. The Institution supplies lawful instructions and obtains any permissions required for students, parents and staff.

Institutional customer data may be hosted, processed, backed up and accessed for support only within the India-only scope agreed in the processing schedule. A service, provider or feature that cannot meet that restriction must remain disabled for that data.

sections.title: 8. Security & Data Protection Reference
sections.html: A summary of our security program, data residency, encryption, and audit practices is available at https://squarecampus.com/security.

sections.title: 9. Service Availability and Maintenance
sections.html:
We aim to offer a reliable Service but cannot guarantee uninterrupted or error-free operation.

Scheduled maintenance or emergency work may temporarily affect availability; we will provide notice where possible.

sections.title: 10. Prohibited Conduct
sections.html:
You must not use the Service to store, share, or process content that is unlawful, harmful, defamatory, obscene, or otherwise objectionable.

  • Infringe third-party rights, including IP or privacy rights;
  • Introduce malware, viruses, or any malicious payload;
  • Engage in conduct prohibited by the Acceptable Use Policy.

sections.title: 11. Term, Suspension, and Termination
sections.html:
Either party may terminate for a material breach the other fails to cure within the reasonable period specified in written notice. SquareCampus may restrict affected access promptly where required by law or needed to contain an immediate threat. For an undisputed overdue payment, it will first give notice and a reasonable opportunity to pay. It will explain the scope where lawful, review the restriction and restore access when its grounds end.

The Institution can discontinue or cancel under its order and the Cancellation and Refund Policy. Suspension or termination does not extinguish return, preservation or deletion duties. Fairhelm will provide a secure handover route even when ordinary user access must end. Confidentiality, accrued payment rights, applicable remedies and data-handling duties survive as needed to give them effect.

sections.title: 12. Intellectual Property
sections.html:
All rights to the Service, interfaces, documentation, and technology belong to SquareCampus or its licensors.

Nothing in these Terms grants you ownership of SquareCampus trademarks, logos, or software.

Each party will use the other’s non-public information only for the agreement and limit access to people who need it and owe confidentiality. This excludes information lawfully public, already lawfully known, independently developed, or lawfully received from another source. Compelled disclosure is limited to what is required, with advance notice where lawful. This duty continues while information remains confidential. Personal data remains protected under applicable law and the DPA.

sections.title: 13. Disclaimers
sections.html: Availability and support commitments expressly stated in the signed order remain binding. Except for those commitments and obligations imposed by law, the Service is supplied as available. The Institution is responsible for professional and educational decisions and for human review of assisted outputs. Nothing in this section displaces the DPA or the express security obligations.

sections.title: 14. Limitation of Liability
sections.html:
Each party is responsible for direct loss caused by its breach, subject to law and reasonable mitigation. Neither party is liable for remote or indirect loss. Reasonable and necessary investigation, restoration and notification costs directly caused by a breach are direct losses.

Except as set out below, each party’s total liability arising from the agreement, including indemnities, is limited to fees paid or payable for the affected order in the twelve months preceding the first event giving rise to the claim. For a complimentary pilot the aggregate cap is ₹50,000 unless the signed order sets a different amount. The order may expressly agree a different cap for a particular risk.

The cap and exclusions do not apply to fraud, wilful misconduct or liability that applicable law prohibits the parties from limiting. The Institution remains responsible for fees properly due. The agreement does not limit a regulator’s powers or an individual’s statutory remedies. A party cannot recover twice for the same loss.

sections.title: 15. Changes to the Terms
sections.html: We identify each revision and will provide material changes to the institutional contact in writing. The signed revision governs the current order unless both parties agree to an amendment or a change is required by law. For a legally required change we will explain the effect and timing as soon as lawful and practicable. Updated commercial terms apply to a new order or an agreed renewal. Opening the app does not amend a school’s signed order.

sections.title: 16. Governing Law and Jurisdiction
sections.html:
These Terms are governed by Indian law, without regard to conflict of law rules.

Subject to mandatory requirements, the courts in Bengaluru, Karnataka, India have exclusive jurisdiction over disputes.

Send contractual notices to the contacts specified in the signed order. For Fairhelm, use legal@squarecampus.com if the order gives no notice address. A waiver must be specific and in writing. If a provision cannot be enforced, the remaining provisions continue to the extent permitted by law.

sections.title: 17. Indemnification
sections.html:
Fairhelm will defend the Institution against third-party claims that the authorised Service infringes intellectual property rights and pay amounts finally awarded or agreed in an approved settlement. This excludes a claim to the extent caused by unauthorised modifications, combinations or institutional material. If continued use is affected, Fairhelm may obtain rights, modify the affected service without material loss of function, or end it and refund prepaid fees for the unserved portion.

The Institution will defend Fairhelm against third-party claims to the extent caused by unlawful material or instructions it supplied, or access it knowingly provided in breach of these Terms. Neither party indemnifies the other for loss caused by the other’s own breach.

The party seeking indemnity must give prompt notice and reasonable cooperation. Delay reduces recovery only to the extent of prejudice. The defending party controls the defence and cannot admit fault for, or impose non-monetary duties on, the other without written consent. Section 14 applies.

sections.title: 18. Security Incident Response
sections.html:
Each party will alert the other without undue delay on learning of a suspected incident affecting the service or institutional records. Use security@squarecampus.com and the Institution’s designated incident contact. Give available facts first, preserve relevant evidence and send updates as facts develop. The DPA sets Fairhelm’s notice and assistance obligations.

Each party must meet its own reporting duties. For incidents listed in the CERT-In Directions, a covered entity must report within six hours of noticing the incident or being informed of it. It must not wait for the other party, a completed investigation or a full written report. Keep applicable ICT logs for the required rolling period. Preserve relevant incident evidence under a documented hold with restricted access, a stated reason and periodic review. Release the hold when the continuing duty ends.

sections.title: 19. Competitor Access Prohibition
sections.html:
The Institution must not give a competing provider access to an account, credentials, private documentation, or confidential screenshots for competitive intelligence or replication. Report suspected unauthorised access promptly. This clause permits ordinary procurement comparisons using public information, independent development, confidential advice from appropriately bound advisers, lawful disclosures and reports to regulators. It grants no third party access to the platform.

For a breach, Fairhelm may contain access, seek appropriate injunctive relief and claim compensation available under Indian law, subject to section 14. Each claim requires a legal basis and the same loss may be recovered only once. The Competitor Notice provides further guidance. In a conflict these Terms govern the Institution’s contractual obligations.

This DPA forms part of every signed SquareCampus pilot or subscription order that incorporates the Terms of Service and involves institutional personal data. The parties must record the applicable revision and complete the processing schedule before live institutional data is submitted. For enquiries, billing and Fairhelm’s own statutory records see the Privacy Policy.

sections.title: 2. Subject Matter and Duration
sections.html:
The Institution instructs Fairhelm to collect, host, organise, retrieve, transmit, secure, return and erase records only as necessary for enabled workflows. The order must identify each enabled purpose, affected people, data categories, duration, approved recipients and providers, processing and support locations, safeguards, contacts and exit arrangements. Written instructions from an identified institutional contact may refine that scope. New purposes require written agreement and lawful authority.

These duties start on receipt of institutional data and continue through return or deletion, including residual backups, even after the order ends.

sections.title: 3. Roles of the Parties
sections.html: The Institution determines the purpose and means of institutional processing as Data Fiduciary. Fairhelm acts as its Data Processor. Fairhelm may process necessary contact, billing and compliance records independently for its own disclosed purposes. It may not repurpose identifiable institutional records for independent analytics, advertising or model training.

sections.title: 4. Categories of Data and Data Subjects
sections.html: The schedule records the actual scope. Examples include applicants’ and students’ admissions, academic, attendance and assessment records, staff identity and payroll metadata, guardian relationships, communications, fees, account identifiers, access events and support records. Photographs, health records and disciplinary records require an expressly authorised purpose, access restrictions and retention instructions. Limit each workflow to the fields it needs.
sections.navigationLabel: Categories of Data and Data Subjects

sections.title: 5. Processor Obligations
sections.html:
Fairhelm will follow lawful documented instructions and promptly flag and pause a disputed instruction it reasonably considers unlawful. For a legally compelled disclosure, it will notify the Institution where lawful, limit disclosure to what is required and record the basis.

Fairhelm will bind authorised personnel to confidentiality, assist with rights requests, incident assessment and applicable regulatory enquiries, and provide evidence reasonably needed to demonstrate compliance. The Institution may review that evidence and, where reasonably necessary, arrange a confidential audit with reasonable notice and safeguards for other institutions. Urgent incidents and regulator deadlines receive priority.

sections.title: 6. Controller Obligations
sections.html:
The Institution supplies lawful, accurate instructions, gives notices, establishes its authority to process, verifies parental or guardian consent where required and documents any purpose-specific exemption. It designates privacy, security and exit contacts, assigns individual credentials and least-privilege roles, reviews access at least quarterly, promptly revokes stale access and records approvals.

Both parties protect credentials, investigate suspected compromise, preserve relevant evidence and cooperate on reasonable remediation. The Institution must promptly escalate changes or withdrawal of authority to Fairhelm. Each party remains responsible for safeguards within its control.

sections.title: 7. Security Measures
sections.html:
Fairhelm will restrict access by role and need, bind support access to authorised purposes, use encryption in transit and at rest, segregate institutional records, log privileged access, monitor for incidents and maintain backup and recovery procedures. Before activation the parties document applicable access controls, recovery arrangements, testing evidence, retention periods and the safeguards required of each provider.

Institutional customer data must remain in India for hosting, processing, backup, recovery and provider or support access. Before enabling a workflow, Fairhelm will document how every provider and access path meets this restriction. A workflow that cannot meet it must remain disabled. Any legally compelled disclosure is handled under section 5.

sections.title: 8. Sub-processors
sections.html:
Before processing, Fairhelm will provide the Institution with the list of providers acting on its behalf, their functions, affected data and processing locations. The agreed schedule authorises those providers. Fairhelm will impose equivalent written obligations and remain responsible for their performance.

Fairhelm will give advance written notice of a proposed addition or replacement and allow a reasonable opportunity to object on documented data-protection grounds. The parties will try to resolve an objection or use an alternative. If they cannot, the Institution may discontinue the affected service and receive unused prepaid fees for it. If an emergency requires an immediate change, Fairhelm will notify the Institution promptly, explain the reason and offer the same remedy. The location and security restrictions apply throughout.

sections.title: 9. Data Subject Requests
sections.html:
Fairhelm will promptly forward requests concerning institutional records to the Institution, preserve the date of receipt and respond directly only on written authority or legal obligation. It will assist in sufficient time for the applicable deadline, including access, correction, withdrawal, erasure, nomination and guardian-authority checks. If a requested operation cannot be completed as instructed, Fairhelm will explain why, propose a lawful alternative and identify any retained copies.

The Institution decides whether an exemption or preservation duty applies. Fairhelm will document completion or the reason for any restriction and pass approved changes to its sub-processors.

sections.title: 10. Data Breach Notification
sections.html:
Fairhelm will alert the institutional incident contact without undue delay on awareness of a suspected or actual compromise affecting institutional personal data. It will give the known time, nature, affected systems, categories and likely impact, mitigation, contact and next update. Missing details will follow as available. It will contain the incident, preserve relevant evidence and provide a closing account of causes and remedial action.

The Institution leads communications to its students, guardians and the Board when acting as Data Fiduciary. Fairhelm will assist. Each party will make any report it is independently required to make, including a CERT-In report within six hours for a listed incident where applicable. Neither party needs the other’s permission to meet a legal deadline. Identify round-the-clock escalation contacts and the initial notice target in the schedule before activation.

sections.title: 11. Data Retention and Deletion
sections.html:
Before activation, agree the record categories, retention instructions and legal holds, exit contact, export scope and format, handover window, any agreed charges, live deletion deadline and maximum backup lifetime. The Institution may elect secure return followed by deletion, or deletion without return. Fairhelm will confirm the election before irreversible deletion and issue written confirmation covering its own systems and sub-processors.

Restricted copies may remain for a documented legal duty or hold, or in isolated backups until scheduled expiry. Specify their purpose, access, review and expiry. If a backup is restored, Fairhelm will reapply deletions and holds before ordinary use. A fee dispute does not cancel return or deletion duties. The Data Retention page explains how an institution can make a request.

sections.title: 12. Priority and Conflicts
sections.html: This DPA controls institutional personal-data processing in a conflict with the Terms or order. A signed amendment must identify the DPA provision it changes. Mandatory law governs throughout. The Terms govern other subjects, including applicable liability and dispute provisions.

sections.title: 13. Governing Law
sections.html: Indian law governs. Subject to mandatory jurisdiction and statutory remedies, the courts in Bengaluru, Karnataka have jurisdiction as provided in the Terms. Send institutional privacy requests to privacy@squarecampus.com and urgent incident notices to security@squarecampus.com.

  • Processing instructions. For each enabled workflow the Institution records the purpose, people, necessary fields, operations and recipients. The Institution approves access and identifies any consent, guardian authority or exemption relied on. Health, disciplinary and other sensitive records require express instructions. Optional AI, messaging and integrations require a named provider, a documented flow and approval before use with institutional records.
  • Application and data storage. Microsoft Azure hosts the tenant application, administrative application and backend API in Central India. The production PostgreSQL database, application blob storage, managed Redis service and monitoring workspace are also provisioned there. The API hostname points to the Central India application environment. The signed order must identify which services will actually receive the Institution’s records, files, session identifiers and diagnostic events.
  • Web delivery and provider access. The tenant and administrative web hostnames use Azure Front Door, a global edge service, with Central India application origins. We have yet to verify an India-only boundary for processing requests and connection metadata at the edge or for provider support access. Section 7 requires these paths to be verified before a workflow carries institutional personal data. The order must identify the contracting provider, downstream providers, permitted support locations and provider-change contact.
  • AI and outbound communications. Microsoft Foundry resources are provisioned in South India. The account contains both regional Standard and Data Zone Standard deployments. Provisioning alone does not establish which model receives a school’s data or where all processing takes place. No AI deployment or external email, SMS or push channel is authorised for institutional records by this schedule. Document the exact service, data, region and retention before adding one.
  • Safeguards. The PostgreSQL configuration requires encrypted transport, uses Microsoft Entra authentication and disables public network access and password authentication. The application blob account uses local redundancy in Central India, encrypted blob storage and HTTPS with a minimum of TLS 1.2. The Institution reviews user access at least quarterly under section 6. Fairhelm and the Institution must name the control owners and record the latest tenant-isolation, access-review and restore evidence for the enabled workflows.
  • Grievances, requests and incidents. The founder handles grievances for Fairhelm. Send privacy requests to privacy@squarecampus.com, operational or exit requests to support@squarecampus.com and urgent security notices to security@squarecampus.com. Fairhelm addresses grievances within one month of receipt, or sooner if required by law. For an incident both parties follow section 10 immediately. The Institution leads communications to its families and regulator where it is the Data Fiduciary. The order must name the institutional contacts, deputies, round-the-clock escalation route, initial notice target and update frequency.
  • Retention and backups. Azure PostgreSQL automated backup retention is configured for seven days with geo-redundant backup disabled. This period applies only to that database backup service. Separate analytics snapshots exist in Central India. The monitoring workspace has a 30-day default and some tables have 90-day retention. The signed schedule must identify the retention trigger and deadline for each record class and the applicable security-log archive, backup expiry and hold process.
  • Return and deletion. The Institution chooses secure return followed by deletion or deletion without return. The order must identify the authorised recipient and secure transfer channel, datasets and attachments, formats, handover window, charges if any, live deletion deadline, and confirmation for providers and restored copies. CSV, XLSX and Parquet are documented for selected backend datasets. Complete pilot export coverage and a maximum lifetime for all residual copies require verification before the parties agree those terms.
  • Approval and changes. Record the approving representatives, dates, order reference and signed revisions. Preserve an exact copy with the completed schedule and record any later changes in writing under section 12.
